title: Afternoon handoff snapshot — ops briefing and follow-ups (2026-03-15 shift)
content:
Shift window: 2026-03-15 14:00 -> 2026-03-15 22:00 UTC
Primary: Marta Alvarez (handoff in)
Secondary: Jordan Kim
Triage scribe: Priya Nair

Executive summary:
- Two medium incidents that impacted tail latency and one isolated GPU OOM on a Dedicated host. No customer data loss. Brief user-facing impact (2–3% increase in 95th percentile latency for hosted text-generation during the spike window).
- Mitigations applied: temporarily rerouted a subset of embeddings traffic away from the misrouted dedicated pool, raised autoscaler floor on dedicated-pool-1 to prevent rapid cold-starts, and restarted ded1-host-03 after graceful drain.
- Outstanding follow-ups and runbook updates assigned below; next shift should validate synthetic test introduced for embeddings route.

Incidents (timeline):
1) 15:07 UTC — embeddings route p95 spike (incident RW-3421)
   - Symptom: p95 for /v1/embeddings spiked from ~120ms to ~780ms for ~18 minutes. Error rate stayed <0.1% but request queuing rose on infer-embed-router.
   - Root cause (hot take): recent routing rule change rolled out at 14:58 (PR 587) caused ~30% of embeddings traffic to be sent to a small Dedicated pool (dedicated-embed-p1) that had lower concurrency and frequent cold starts. The combination caused queueing and upstream load on cache tier.
   - Immediate mitigation: rolled routing change back at 15:12 and enabled a temporary sticky route to hosted-embed-backend for new sessions; increased dedicated-embed-p1 minimum instances to 3 (was 1) to avoid cold-start thundering.
   - Post-shift actions: add a rollout-check in the deploy pipeline to fail when target pool capacity < X. Assign: Jordan K., due 2026-03-18.

2) 17:34 UTC — KV cache eviction storm causing random downstream latency (informal RW-3421a)
   - Symptom: sudden cache miss rate increase for key-prefix 'chat:kv:' correlated with a background job that ran shard compaction in the cache tier. Overall tokens/sec stayed stable but p99 for streaming chat increased to ~2.1s from usual ~700ms for ~25 minutes.
   - Mitigation: disabled compaction job scope, warmed cache by replaying hot prefix set from metrics snapshot, and throttled compaction to run in smaller batches.
   - Next steps: draft runbook entry for safe compaction window and add guard that aborts compaction if miss_rate rises > 3x baseline. Assign: Priya N., due 2026-03-19.

3) 19:50 UTC — ded1-host-03 GPU OOM (isolated)
   - Symptom: single host returned OOM from CUDA runtime during a long-context request (seq_len=32k) on a non-production replica. Host auto-evacuated and unhealthy flag tripped. No customer traffic was routed to it at the time.
   - Mitigation: drained and restarted the host; kernel logs attached to ticket; coordinated with infra to reimage if flakiness recurs.
   - Follow-up: add stricter mem-limit guard for large sequence inference and add an automated alert when the host reports >80% GPU memory for >30s. Assign: Liam O., due 2026-03-17.

Operational notes and ad hoc observations:
- Observability: Graph dashboard for embeddings p95 lacked annotation for the 14:58 routing change. Please annotate RW-3421 on the embeddings dashboard to aid future triage.
- Cost/control: raising the minimum instance for dedicated-embed-p1 increased short-term cost; finance aware but acceptable impact for availability.
- Behavioural: some alerts are still too chatty during autoscale events (see alert group: infra/autoscaler/noise). Suggest consolidating autoscale start/stop alerts with a 2-minute suppression window. Assign: Jordan K., due 2026-03-20.

Runbook draft notes (items to add or change) – please review before next deploy:
- Embeddings routing rollout checklist: verify target pool capacity >= expected RPS/10, synthetic load test pass, and run canary for at least 5 minutes.
- KV compaction safe window: only run between 03:00–06:00 UTC by default; abort if miss_rate growth > 200% in 5m.
- Large-sequence inference guard: automatically route sequence-length > 8k to specialized large-context pool or reject with 413 + guidance.

Action items (concise):
- RW-3421 Jira ticket: post-incident summary + timeline (owner: Marta A., due 2026-03-17)
- Add rollout-check in infra deploy (owner: Jordan K., RW-3435, due 2026-03-18)
- KV compaction guard + runbook page update (owner: Priya N., RW-3436, due 2026-03-19)
- GPU memory alert + memory-guard enforcement (owner: Liam O., RW-3437, due 2026-03-17)
- Dashboard annotation and alert suppression change (owner: Jordan K., due 2026-03-20)

Notes to next shift (short):
- Check embeddings synthetic test (theta-synth-embed) running in prod namespace; it should be green. If failing, do not deploy any routing changes until green.
- Monitor dedicated pool sizes — autoscaler logs indicate one instance flapped twice around 15:10; check for spikes in churn.
- Confirm that ded1-host-03 remains stable after restart; watch for repeated OOMs and attach GPU logs to RW-3437.

Miscellaneous housekeeping:
- PR 587 (infra) reverted; will land again only after rollout-check PR.
- Confluence: initial draft of KV compaction runbook is at https://confluence.redwood/display/SRE/kv-cache-runbook — please comment inline.
- Slack: thread #sre-ops-RW-3421 summarizes real-time comms; tag @oncall-next if you need escalation.

Post-shift retrospective notes (quick):
- The change that caused routing to misdirect traffic should have been caught by the deploy-time capacity guard; add this as a blocker for rolling changes that touch routing.
- Observability gaps (missing deploy annotations and no synthetic test for embeddings until now) increased mean time to mitigation. Synthetic test was introduced during the shift; verify its schedule and reliable alerting.

Handoff acceptance checklist (next shift):
- [ ] Confirm RW-3421 ticket has initial post-incident writeup.
- [ ] Validate theta-synth-embed is passing.
- [ ] Confirm ded1-host-03 gpu memory stable for 2 hours.
- [ ] Check PR 587 status and rollout-check PR progress.

If anything is blocking you when taking this over, ping oncall and escalate to SRE lead (Lina Park) if customer-facing latency > 5% for > 30 minutes.

Signed off by: Marta Alvarez (oncall), 2026-03-16 03:45 UTC

Attachments and logs: see linked_artifacts above and ticket RW-3421 for raw flamegraphs, router logs, and kube events.
